reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Standing to bring actions on claims arising under foreign law
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes suits on claims under another state's law by persons entitled to proceeds or by foreign-empowered representative fiduciaries.

headings.title: Receipt and distribution of proceeds by representative
headings.reviewNote: Empowers representative plaintiffs to satisfy judgments, execute releases, and distribute proceeds under the governing laws of the other state.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections and Huff v. LaSieur (571 S.W.2d 654) annotation on standing to sue on claims under another state's law and representative proceeds distribution.

headings.title: Joinder of persons having joint interest
headings.reviewNote: Mandates joinder of parties with joint interests, permitting an unwilling plaintiff to be joined as a defendant.

headings.title: Court order adding necessary parties for complete controversy
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to order necessary additional parties brought in by amended or supplemental petition when complete relief requires them.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections and cross-references (431.140, 509.470) on mandatory joinder of joint-interest parties and adding necessary parties.

headings.title: Permissive joinder of parties and separate incident restriction
headings.reviewNote: Governs permissive joinder of plaintiffs and defendants sharing common questions, expressly excluding separate purchases or incidents involving same products.

headings.title: Legislative adoption of judicial holding on joinder and venue
headings.reviewNote: Codifies the Missouri Supreme Court holding in State ex rel. Johnson & Johnson v. Burlison concerning joinder and venue limits.

headings.title: Protective orders and separate trials to prevent prejudice
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court orders for separate trials or other relief to prevent party embarrassment, delay, or expense from permissive joinder.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections and Burlison (567 S.W.3d 168) annotation on permissive joinder, separate product purchase/incident bar, Burlison adoption, and separate trials.

headings.title: Misjoinder not grounds for dismissal and party severance
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that misjoinder does not warrant dismissal and permits parties to be added, dropped, or claims severed by court order.

headings.title: Timing of motions to drop or add parties
headings.reviewNote: Governs the timing and procedure for making motions to drop or add parties concurrently with responsive motions under section 509.290.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on non-dismissal for misjoinder, dropping/adding/severing parties, and timing of motions with section 509.290/509.340 rules.

headings.title: Interpleader joinder of adverse claimants exposing plaintiff to multiple liability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes interpleader joinder when competing claims against a plaintiff or insured expose them to multiple liability.

headings.title: Definition of plaintiff insurer or public risk pool
headings.reviewNote: Defines plaintiff for interpleader liability limitations to include insurers, public entity risk pools, and municipal self-insurance arrangements.

headings.title: Definition of claim against plaintiff or insured
headings.reviewNote: Defines claim to include all actual or potential claims asserted against an insurer or insured arising out of an event.

headings.title: Insurer liability limit upon timely interpleader filing
headings.reviewNote: Limits an insurer's liability to available policy coverage if interpleader is initiated within ninety days of the first settlement demand.

headings.title: Retention of underlying damages claims against insured
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that interpleader by an insurer does not require dismissal or release of damages claims against the insured tortfeasor.

headings.title: Preservation of insured defense control and consent rights
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the insured's contractual or legal rights to consent to settlements or control the defense of claims.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections on interpleader joinder, insurer/risk pool definitions, 90-day timely interpleader liability cap, underlying claims, and insured defense/consent rights.

headings.title: Class action prerequisites and representative capacity
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes criteria for class representation when persons are numerous, defining joint, common, secondary, and severable rights.

headings.title: Shareholder derivative actions and demand requirements
headings.reviewNote: Sets pleading requirements for shareholder derivative actions, including contemporaneous ownership and efforts to obtain redress from directors or shareholders.

headings.title: Court approval and notice for class action dismissal or compromise
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits dismissal or compromise of class actions without court approval and requires notice to class members.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections on class action prerequisites, shareholder derivative pleading/demand requirements, and court approval/notice for dismissal or compromise.

headings.title: Third-party practice by defendant against nonparty
headings.reviewNote: Governs third-party summons and petition practice by defendants against nonparties potentially liable for all or part of the plaintiff's claim.

headings.title: Third-party practice by plaintiff upon counterclaim
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a plaintiff to bring in a third party when a counterclaim is asserted against that plaintiff.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections governing third-party practice by defendants and by plaintiffs facing counterclaims.

headings.title: Mandatory intervention of right in civil actions
headings.reviewNote: Identifies circumstances where intervention of right must be granted, including statutory rights and adverse effects on property or representation.

headings.title: Permissive intervention upon conditional statutory right or common question
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes permissive intervention in the court's discretion upon conditional statutory authority or common questions of law or fact.

headings.title: Motion procedure and pleading requirements for intervention
headings.reviewNote: Specifies procedural requirements for intervention, requiring service of a motion stating grounds accompanied by the proposed pleading.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections and In re Matter of Trapp (595 S.W.2d 193) annotation on intervention of right, permissive intervention, motion procedure, and state/subdivision notice.

headings.title: Party substitution upon death and suggestion of death
headings.reviewNote: Governs party substitution upon death, survival to remaining parties, and dismissal if substitution is not moved within nine months after first published notice of letters.

headings.title: Party substitution upon mental incapacity
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes continuation of an action by or against the legal representative upon a party's mental incapacity.

headings.title: Substitution or joinder upon transfer of interest
headings.reviewNote: Permits an action to proceed with the original party or directs substitution or joinder of the transferee upon transfer of interest.

headings.title: Party substitution upon corporate dissolution or charter forfeiture
headings.reviewNote: Provides for continuation of pending litigation by or against statutory trustees upon corporate dissolution or charter forfeiture.

headings.title: Substitution of successor public officers upon motion
headings.reviewNote: Permits continuing an action by or against a successor public officer upon motion within one year with reasonable notice and opportunity to object, or court appointment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections; corrected subsection 1 note from 90 days to 9 months after published letters notice and revised subsection 5 title to remove erroneous "Automatic".

headings.title: Bond requirement for next friend or guardian ad litem
headings.reviewNote: Requires approved bond before a next friend or guardian ad litem receives money or property, permitting court waiver for minor amounts.

headings.title: Double penal liability and void releases for failure to post bond
headings.reviewNote: Renders a next friend or guardian ad litem who receives minor funds without an approved bond personally liable for double value and voids any release, receipt, or satisfaction.

headings.title: Duration of fiduciary duties and bond obligations
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that next friend duties and surety bond obligations continue until formal court discharge.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections; replaced mismatched subsection 2 heading to accurately reflect double penal liability and void releases for failing to execute a bond.

headings.title: Authority to waive jury trial on behalf of minor
headings.reviewNote: Empowers a next friend, guardian ad litem, or conservator to waive jury trial and submit issues to the court subject to judicial approval.

headings.title: Settlement contracting authority and fee agreements
headings.reviewNote: Grants authority to contract for claim settlement and attorney representation on behalf of a minor, subject to court approval.

headings.title: Judicial hearing and approval of minor claim settlements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to hear evidence and approve or disapprove proposed settlement contracts affecting minor claims.

headings.title: Exemption for minor claim settlements under section 436.700
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section neither prohibits settlements under section 436.700 nor requires court approval of settlements executed under section 436.700.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections and Bailey/Holoman/Arthur annotations; corrected subsection 4 title/note from "structured settlement" to minor claim settlements under section 436.700.

headings.title: Substitution of appointed conservator for next friend or GAL
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a minor's appointed conservator to be substituted as party for a next friend or guardian ad litem upon court order.

headings.title: Binding effect of preexisting contracts on substituted conservator
headings.reviewNote: Enforces valid pre-substitution attorney fee and expense contracts against a substituted conservator unless previously approved or altered.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on ex parte substitution of a minor's conservator for next friend or GAL and binding effect of court-approved attorney fee contracts.

headings.title: Disposition of minor proceeds equal to or under ten thousand dollars
headings.reviewNote: Governs court disposition of minor proceeds of ten thousand dollars or less under probate alternatives and discharge of fiduciary upon filed receipt.

headings.title: Transfer of minor proceeds exceeding ten thousand dollars to conservator
headings.reviewNote: Mandates transfer of minor net proceeds exceeding ten thousand dollars to a qualified conservator and provides for fiduciary discharge.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections governing disposition of net minor proceeds ($10,000 or less under section 475.330 vs over $10,000 to conservator) and fiduciary discharge.

headings.title: Motion by city of over 150,000 to join coresponsible parties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes cities over 150,000 sued for wrongful or negligent acts of third parties to notify plaintiffs to join those parties as defendants.

headings.title: Mandatory joinder procedure, motion to strike, and unserved parties
headings.reviewNote: Outlines joinder procedures, motions to strike notice, and conditions allowing plaintiff to proceed against the city alone if process cannot be served.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on motions by cities over 150,000 to require joinder of coresponsible third parties, motions to strike, and unserved-party exception.
